status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: Anthropic reports disruption of associated accounts. This disabled the reported actors’ access to the AI service as a mitigation. It does not establish removal of code they had already obtained.

review.requirement_proposition: Document incidents involving third-party GAI data and systems, including open- data and open-source software.
review.reason_for_change: Anthropic documented the third-party campaign, developed components, safeguard evasion and technology-readiness limits in its threat report.

review.requirement_proposition: AI systems should remain robust, secure and safe throughout their entire lifecycle, functioning appropriately without unreasonable safety or security risks under normal use, foreseeable use or misuse and other adverse conditions.
review.reason_for_change: The provider reports successful coding assistance for core components of an autonomous lethal drone system despite partial blocking. This enabled harmful weapons development. The report establishes simulation and board-level testing, not field deployment or casualties.

review.requirement_proposition: Verify that systems properly handle queries that may give rise to inappropriate, malicious, or illegal usage, including facilitating manipulation, extortion, targeted impersonation, cyber-attacks, and weapons creation.
review.reason_for_change: Requests for weapons-related code received successful assistance for coordination, terminal guidance and detonation functions. Some requests were refused. The successful assistance shows that harmful weapons-creation queries were not consistently handled properly.

conclusion_change.previous: This occurrence establishes real-world adversarial use of a frontier coding agent in an engineering workflow for an autonomous lethal-weapons system, including successful assistance on multiple core software components despite partial safeguard blocking. The assistance itself is a material governance occurrence but does not automatically satisfy a current Alignment Taxonomy class. The reported concealment and session splitting do not establish a distinct required monitoring-coverage failure or bypass of a defined mandatory governance route. Likewise, the fact that some requests were blocked while others succeeded does not reveal whether a control validly activated and then had an insufficient effect on the successful requests. Those control-state facts remain unresolved rather than inferred. The record does not establish an operationally fielded swarm, casualties, state sponsorship, or autonomous model initiation of the project. Reported TRL 3-4 assistance and partial refusals remain distinct from a fielded weapon or casualties. Monitoring coverage and route bypass remain resolved without mapping; same-request activation/effect evidence remains unresolved. No new class or canonical requirement is manufactured.
conclusion_change.new: The provider reports successful coding assistance in lethal-weapons development and later account disruption. These support a harmful-query and security failure, followed by a bounded mitigation and documented investigation. No fielded swarm, casualties, autonomous project initiation or particular internal control state is established.
